{"parentUuid":"bb5b58cd-37ff-40ac-a756-db1f8203d828","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"mcp_instructions_delta","addedNames":["claude.ai Claude Docs"],"addedBlocks":["## claude.ai Claude Docs\nClaude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = [\"topic.index\"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {\"kind\":\"project\",\"create\":{\"name\":\"<title>\",\"doc\":{\"blocks\":{\"asof\":{\"type\":\"date\",\"value\":\"<today>\"},\"me\":{\"type\":\"mention\",\"user\":\"me\"},\"s1\":{\"type\":\"pending\",\"intent\":\"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to\"},\"s2\":{…}},\"markdown\":\"# <title>\\n\\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\\n\\n<?claude block s1?>\\n\\n<?claude block s2?>\"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = [\"topic.index\"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: \"<root id>\"`."],"removedNames":[]},"type":"attachment","uuid":"15c8c2de-3101-4075-827d-e01dbe55ed73","timestamp":"2026-10-13T14:28:25.175Z","rendered":[{"content":"<system-reminder>\n# MCP Server Instructions\n\nThe following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:\n\n## claude.ai Claude Docs\nClaude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = [\"topic.index\"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {\"kind\":\"project\",\"create\":{\"name\":\"<title>\",\"doc\":{\"blocks\":{\"asof\":{\"type\":\"date\",\"value\":\"<today>\"},\"me\":{\"type\":\"mention\",\"user\":\"me\"},\"s1\":{\"type\":\"pending\",\"intent\":\"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to\"},\"s2\":{…}},\"markdown\":\"# <title>\\n\\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\\n\\n<?claude block s1?>\\n\\n<?claude block s2?>\"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = [\"topic.index\"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: \"<root id>\"`.\n</system-reminder>"}],"renderedRole":"system","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maysg/orca/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"91f90b48-e4a0-44e0-aa4c-47594fc96da9","version":"2.1.296","gitBranch":"main"}
{"parentUuid":"15c8c2de-3101-4075-827d-e01dbe55ed73","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like \"how do I do X\", \"find a skill for X\", \"is there a skill that can...\", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.\n- mattpocock-skills:diagnosing-bugs: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says \"diagnose\"/\"debug this\", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.\n- mattpocock-skills:tdd: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions \"red-green-refactor\", or wants integration tests.\n- mattpocock-skills:prototype: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.\n- mattpocock-skills:research: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.\n- mattpocock-skills:domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a CONTEXT.md, or recording or editing an ADR.\n- mattpocock-skills:codebase-design: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.\n- mattpocock-skills:code-review: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to \"review since X\".\n- mattpocock-skills:resolving-merge-conflicts: Use when you need to resolve an in-progress git merge/rebase conflict.\n- mattpocock-skills:wizard: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.\n- mattpocock-skills:grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.\n- mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.\n- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: \"chart\", \"graph\", \"plot\", \"data viz\", \"visualization\", \"dashboard\", \"analytics\", \"visualize data\", \"categorical colors\", \"sequential / diverging palette\", \"stat tile\", \"sparkline\", \"heatmap\", \"legend\", \"axis\", \"tooltip\", \"chart colors\", \"color by series\".\n- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.\n- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.\n- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, handing the viewer a file to save, or using the viewer's camera, microphone, location, screen or device motion. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.\n- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.\n- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.\nTRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it \"looks like a one-liner\" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).\nSKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).\n- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.\n- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).\n- plugin-authoring: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a live pane or panel, a band above the prompt, a status line, a toast, a slash command, or a hook on tool calls or prompts. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.\n- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation\n- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch\n- anthropic-skills:built-in-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or \"your own browser\"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.\n- anthropic-skills:chrome-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.\n- anthropic-skills:computer-use: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for \"computer use\". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills.\n- anthropic-skills:deep-research: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly.\n- anthropic-skills:docs: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.\n- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.\n- anthropic-skills:google-workspace: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even \"change it\" or \"add a tab\". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.\n- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.\n- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.\n- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.\n- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.\n- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.\n- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like \"the xlsx in my downloads\") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. {"parentUuid":"1f011dda-20a4-4328-9bcb-218d7cab119b","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"b166393f-ae29-48ab-a7bb-82b437a312be","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01JcDBmmi1r6HjXsW85tDyjT","type":"tool_result","content":"title:\tT06: Dashboard and content list\nstate:\tOPEN\nauthor:\tMaysG-creator\nlabels:\tready-for-agent, ticket\ncomments:\t0\nassignees:\t\nprojects:\t\nmilestone:\t\nissue-type:\t\nparent:\t\nsub-issues:\t\nsub-issues-completed:\t\nblocked-by:\t\nblocking:\t\nnumber:\t7\n--\n## Parent\n\nSpec: #1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe admin console gets a dashboard that shows counts (drafts, published updates, pages) and a content list of updates and pages that can be filtered by status and by type, for both admin and editor.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] The dashboard shows counts of drafts, published updates, and pages that match the data\n- [ ] The content list shows updates and pages together with title, type, status, author, and last-updated date\n- [ ] The list filters by status (draft or published) and by type (update or page), and the filters combine\n- [ ] A filter with no matches shows a clear empty message\n- [ ] Both admin and editor can see the dashboard and list, and anonymous visitors are redirected to login\n- [ ] The dashboard and list fit 390 px wide with no sideways scrolling\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #6 (T05: Pages with nav order)\n\n# CONTEXT.md glossary\n\nClient: Kenyon College Men's Soccer. The site is run by student media members so fans,\nalumni, and players' families can find accurate game info without digging through Instagram.\n\nUse these words everywhere (code, templates, tickets, commits). If a better word appears,\nchange it here instead of using both.\n\n## Terms\n\n**Update** — A time-ordered team news item (what the CMS stores as a *post*). Free-form\nMarkdown with a title. Never call it \"article\" or \"bulletin\". Shown newest first on the home page.\n\n**Fixture** — A scheduled game, listed on the Schedule page. Fans may say \"game\" or \"match\";\nthe glossary term is *fixture*.\n\n**Match report** — An *update* written after a fixture, holding the verified score and scorers.\nAlso called a recap.\n\n**Page** — Stable content that appears in the public navigation: Schedule, Roster,\nResults/Record, History, About/Contact.\n\n**Nav order** — A number on each *page* set by the admin that decides where it sits in the\npublic menu. Schedule and Results come before History and About.\n\n**History** — A *page* covering the program's past titles and accomplishments.\n\n**Draft** — Content only visible in the admin console. Editors can only produce drafts.\nDrafts never reach `site/`.\n\n**Published** — Content that `cms publish` exports to the public site. Only the admin can set it.\n\n**Slug** — URL-safe name generated from the title when first saved. Read-only for editors.\n\n**Admin** — The single account that publishes, deletes published content, manages users, and\nruns `cms publish` and `cms deploy`. Exactly one exists at any time.\n\n**Editor** — A student media member. Creates and edits drafts, edits any draft, deletes only\ntheir own drafts, and cannot change published content.\n\n**Hand-over** — The admin action that promotes another user to admin and demotes the current\nadmin in one step. It's the only way the admin role changes hands.\n\n**Last updated** — The date shown on every public update and page, so fans can judge freshness.\n\n## Decisions\n\n- Out of scope: comments, live scores, WYSIWYG editor, multi-site.\n- Stretch (after the 7 core capabilities): photo uploads with alt text, categories and tags.\n- The admin console runs on one machine; remote access for editors comes later.\n- Updates are expected about an hour after a game, not live.\n- The home page orders updates by when they were first written, newest first. Editing or\n  correcting an update changes its *last updated* date but never moves it above a newer update.\n- The public site is purple and white with a CSS-only banner. The admin console is not themed.\n- Sample content is clearly marked as sample, never invented scores or stats.\n- A deactivated user keeps their authorship and content.\napp\nCLAUDE.md\ncms.db\nCONTEXT.md\ndocs\nnotes\npyproject.toml\nREADME.md\nscripts\nSECURITY-CHECKLIST.md\nsite\ntemplates\ntests\nuv.lock\n# Issue tracker: GitHub\n\nIssues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\n- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.\n- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. The site is run by student media members so fans,\nalumni, and players' families can find accurate game info without digging through Instagram.\n\nUse these words everywhere (code, templates, tickets, commits). If a better word appears,\nchange it here instead of using both.\n\n## Terms\n\n**Update** — A time-ordered team news item (what the CMS stores as a *post*). Free-form\nMarkdown with a title. Never call it \"article\" or \"bulletin\". Shown newest first on the home page.\n\n**Fixture** — A scheduled game, listed on the Schedule page. Fans may say \"game\" or \"match\";\nthe glossary term is *fixture*.\n\n**Match report** — An *update* written after a fixture, holding the verified score and scorers.\nAlso called a recap.\n\n**Page** — Stable content that appears in the public navigation: Schedule, Roster,\nResults/Record, History, About/Contact.\n\n**Nav order** — A number on each *page* set by the admin that decides where it sits in the\npublic menu. Schedule and Results come before History and About.\n\n**History** — A *page* covering the program's past titles and accomplishments.\n\n**Draft** — Content only visible in the admin console. Editors can only produce drafts.\nDrafts never reach `site/`.\n\n**Published** — Content that `cms publish` exports to the public site. Only the admin can set it.\n\n**Slug** — URL-safe name generated from the title when first saved. Read-only for editors.\n\n**Admin** — The single account that publishes, deletes published content, manages users, and\nruns `cms publish` and `cms deploy`. Exactly one exists at any time.\n\n**Editor** — A student media member. Creates and edits drafts, edits any draft, deletes only\ntheir own drafts, and cannot change published content.\n\n**Hand-over** — The admin action that promotes another user to admin and demotes the current\nadmin in one step. It's the only way the admin role changes hands.\n\n**Last updated** — The date shown on every public update and page, so fans can judge freshness.\n\n## Decisions\n\n- Out of scope: comments, live scores, WYSIWYG editor, multi-site.\n- Stretch (after the 7 core capabilities): photo uploads with alt text, categories and tags.\n- The admin console runs on one machine; remote access for editors comes later.\n- Updates are expected about an hour after a game, not live.\n- The home page orders updates by when they were first written, newest first. Editing or\n  correcting an update changes its *last updated* date but never moves it above a newer update.\n- The public site is purple and white with a CSS-only banner. The admin console is not themed.\n- Sample content is clearly marked as sample, never invented scores or stats.\n- A deactivated user keeps their authorship and content.\napp\nCLAUDE.md\ncms.db\nCONTEXT.md\ndocs\nnotes\npyproject.toml\nREADME.md\nscripts\nSECURITY-CHECKLIST.md\nsite\ntemplates\ntests\nuv.lock\n# Issue tracker: GitHub\n\nIssues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\n- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.\n\nDon't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.\n\n## The reason field\n\nOne short sentence on what you chose and why. {"parentUuid":"09f48cdd-38a3-437c-9485-e406f9f1e9d3","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"b166393f-ae29-48ab-a7bb-82b437a312be","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_012cL67gBPcF37FLnogjEjDY","type":"tool_result","content":"title:\tSpec: Kenyon Men's Soccer CMS\nstate:\tOPEN\nauthor:\tMaysG-creator\nlabels:\tready-for-agent, spec\ncomments:\t0\nassignees:\t\nprojects:\t\nmilestone:\t\nissue-type:\t\nparent:\t\nsub-issues:\t\nsub-issues-completed:\t\nblocked-by:\t\nblocking:\t\nnumber:\t1\n--\n## Problem Statement\n\nKenyon College Men's Soccer has no reliable place for fans, alumni, and players' families to find accurate game information. Today news comes through Instagram, which is hard to search and confusing for older relatives, and updates arrive in a random order. The team's student media members have average computer skills and need a simple way to write updates, but a wrong score or scorer on a public team site is worse than no site at all. The program needs a small CMS where several students can prepare content, one trusted person decides what goes public, and fans see a fast, readable, purple and white site that says when it was last updated.\n\n## Solution\n\nA local admin console (FastAPI, Jinja, SQLite) where one admin and a group of student editors log in, write updates and pages, and manage users, plus a `cms publish` step that exports only published content as static HTML for GitHub Pages. Editors can only produce drafts; the single admin reviews and publishes. The public site shows the newest updates on the home page, a navigation built from published pages (Schedule, Roster, Results/Record, History, About/Contact), and a last-updated date on everything. The admin console never goes on the internet.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As an editor, I want to log in with my own email and password, so that my work is attributed to me.\n2. As an editor, I want a clear message when my password is wrong, so that I know to retry rather than think the site is broken.\n3. As an admin, I want to log out, so that nobody else can use the shared machine under my name.\n4. As an editor, I want to log out, so that the next editor at the shared machine signs in as themselves.\n5. As an admin, I want every password stored only as a hash, so that a stolen database never reveals passwords.\n6. As an editor, I want to create an update with a title and a Markdown body, so that I can write up a game quickly.\n7. As an editor, I want the slug generated from the title automatically, so that I never have to think about URLs.\n8. As an editor, I want a duplicate slug to be resolved automatically, so that two updates with the same title do not collide.\n9. As an editor, I want a Markdown preview in the editor, so that I can check formatting before I save.\n10. As an editor, I want my new content saved as a draft, so that nothing reaches fans before the admin approves it.\n11. As an editor, I want to edit any draft, so that a teammate can fix a mistake on game night.\n12. As an editor, I want to delete my own drafts, so that abandoned drafts do not clutter the list.\n13. As an editor, I want to be blocked from deleting someone else's draft, so that nobody loses work by accident.\n14. As an editor, I want to be blocked from publishing, unpublishing, or editing published content, so that live content only changes with the admin's approval.\n15. As an editor, I want a clear \"not allowed\" screen when I try an admin-only action, so that I understand why it did not work.\n16. As an editor, I want to create and edit page drafts such as Schedule, Roster, or History, so that I can prepare content for the admin.\n17. As an editor, I want to filter the content list by status and by type, so that I can find drafts that need work.\n18. As an editor, I want a success or error message after every save, so that I know whether my change landed.\n19. As an editor, I want the admin navigation visible on every screen, so that I never get lost.\n20. As an admin, I want a dashboard showing counts of drafts, published updates, and pages, so that I see what needs review at a glance.\n21. As an admin, I want to filter the content list to drafts, so that I can review what editors wrote.\n22. As an admin, I want to publish a draft, so that it becomes eligible for the public site.\n23. As an admin, I want to unpublish published content, so that a wrong score can be pulled quickly.\n24. As an admin, I want to edit published content, so that I can correct a mistake.\n25. As an admin, I want to delete published content or pages, with a confirm step, so that I do not remove something live by accident.\n26. As an admin, I want to set each page's nav order, so that Schedule and Results appear before History and About.\n27. As an admin, I want to create a user with an email, a name, a role, and a starting password, so that a new media member can join.\n28. As an admin, I want to change a user's role, so that responsibilities can change.\n29. As an admin, I want to deactivate a user, so that a graduating media member can no longer log in.\n30. As a deactivated user, I want my past drafts and attribution kept, so that history is not rewritten.\n31. As an admin, I want the system to enforce exactly one admin, so that the club's single-admin rule is true in code.\n32. As an admin, I want a hand-over action that promotes another user and demotes me in one step, so that the role can pass on when I graduate.\n33. As an admin, I want to be prevented from deactivating or demoting myself outside of hand-over, so that the site is never left without an admin.\n34. As an admin, I want `cms publish` to render only published updates and pages, so that drafts never leave the database.\n35. As an admin, I want `cms publish` to remove content I unpublished or deleted from the exported site, so that stale content does not stay live.\n36. As an admin, I want `cms deploy` to push the export to the gh-pages branch, so that fans see the new content.\n37. As an admin, I want a short written runbook for publish and deploy, so that whoever inherits the role can do it.\n38. As a fan, I want the home page to list the newest published updates first with their dates, so that I see the latest news.\n39. As a fan, I want a navigation menu built from published pages, so that I can reach Schedule, Roster, Results, History, and About.\n40. As a fan, I want each update and page to show when it was last updated, so that I can judge whether it is current.\n41. As a fan, I want to read a match report with the verified score and scorers, so that I trust the numbers.\n42. As an alumnus, I want a History page about past titles and accomplishments, so that I can find the program's record.\n43. As a player's relative, I want a Roster page, so that I can find the player.\n44. As a fan on a phone, I want the public site and admin screens to fit without sideways scrolling, so that I can read them anywhere.\n45. As a fan, I want the site to look purple and white with a clear header, so that it feels like Kenyon.\n46. As any visitor, I want all links to work on the hosted site, so that I never hit a broken page.\n47. As any visitor, I want no script from a user's Markdown to run, so that the site is safe to open.\n48. As the admin, I want every state-changing form to carry a CSRF token, so that another website cannot act on my behalf.\n49. As a maintainer, I want sample content clearly marked as sample, so that no invented score ever looks real.\n50. As an anonymous visitor to the admin console, I want to be sent to the login page, so that nothing is exposed.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Architecture.** Follow ADR-001 and ADR-002: a local FastAPI app with server-rendered Jinja templates and SQLite, and a publish step that writes static HTML. No frontend framework and no build step.\n- **Vocabulary.** All code, templates, and tickets use the terms in `CONTEXT.md`: Update (stored as a post), Fixture, Match report, Page, Nav order, Draft, Published, Slug, Admin, Editor, Hand-over, Last updated.\n- **Users.** A user has an email, a display name, a password hash (argon2), a role (admin or editor), and an active flag. Deactivation sets the flag and never deletes the user, so authorship survives.\n- **Single admin.** Exactly one active admin exists at all times. Role changes cannot create a second admin, and the admin cannot demote or deactivate themselves. The only path is a hand-over action, which promotes the target and demotes the current admin atomically.\n- **Content.** Updates and Pages share the same core fields: title, slug, Markdown body, status (draft or published), author, created and updated timestamps. Pages add a nav order. Only two statuses exist.\n- **Slugs.** Generated from the title on first save, made unique automatically, and not editable by editors. Only the admin may change a slug.\n- **Permissions.** Editor: create content as drafts, edit any draft, delete own drafts, view the content list and dashboard. Editor may not publish, unpublish, edit or delete published content, delete another editor's draft, or reach user management. Admin: everything, including publish, unpublish, edit and delete published content, and user management. Admin-only routes return 403 for editors and redirect anonymous visitors to login.\n- **Session and login.** Cookie-based sessions. Login failures show one generic message. Deactivated users cannot log in.\n- **CSRF.** Every state-changing form carries a token that the server verifies, and a POST without a valid token is rejected.\n- **Markdown safety.** User Markdown is rendered and then sanitized with an allow-list, both in the admin preview and in the export, so script tags and event-handler attributes never execute.\n- **Admin console.** A dashboard with counts, a filterable content list (by status and by type), an editor with a Markdown preview, a user list, and persistent navigation. Every save shows a success or error message. The console is not themed beyond clear, plain styling.\n- **Publish.** `cms publish` reads only published rows and regenerates the export folder from scratch, so unpublished or deleted content disappears. Output uses relative paths only. The home page lists published updates newest first, the navigation is built from published pages by nav order, and each item shows its last-updated date. `cms deploy` pushes the export to the gh-pages branch. Both commands run from the terminal, and a short runbook is part of the documentation.\n- **Public look.** Purple and white, with a CSS-only banner header, readable at 390 px. No image files are required.\n- **Seed data.** The demo seed creates one admin, one editor, a few drafts, and a few published items. All content is clearly marked as sample, never realistic scores or stats. Credentials come from the environment.\n- **Assumptions.** A deactivated user keeps authorship and content. Updates are expected about an hour after a game. Editors use one shared machine for now.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- **What a good test is.** It asserts external behavior only: a status code, a redirect, a page's visible text, a file in the export. It never asserts on internal functions, table layouts, or template structure.\n- **Seam 1: the HTTP app.** Every capability is tested through the FastAPI test client, using the existing `client` and `client_as(role)` helpers. This covers login and logout, roles and the editor 403 and anonymous redirect on every admin-only route, content CRUD and status changes, the dashboard and filters, preview, user management, hand-over, CSRF rejection, and sanitized preview output.\n- **Seam 2: the publish export.** Run the exporter into a temporary folder and assert on the generated files: only published content is present, drafts are absent, unpublished content disappears on re-export, no root-absolute paths, navigation order matches nav order, sanitized bodies, and a last-updated date on each item.\n- **Acceptance criteria.** Each ticket's acceptance criteria map to at least one named test so the review and grading can trace them.\n- **Prior art.** The template's existing T00 test and the `client_as` fixture and its docstring examples for access-control tests.\n- **Not tested.** Visual styling and the GitHub deploy itself are checked by hand and with screenshots at 1280 px and 390 px.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Comments and moderation.\n- Live in-game scores or any server-side feature on the public site.\n- WYSIWYG editors, drag-and-drop page builders, and multi-site.\n- Remote access for editors; for now the console runs on one machine (a later change, possibly the live admin deploy stretch).\n- A \"verified result\" workflow or required source field for scores.\n- Theming the admin console.\n- Photo uploads and categories/tags are wanted but not in the core build; see Further Notes.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- **Stretch goals, after the 7 core capabilities are green and reviewed:** photo uploads with alt text, and categories and tags (for example by season or opponent). Each gets its own `stretch` issue. Today news comes through Instagram, which is hard to search and confusing for older relatives, and updates arrive in a random order. The team's student media members have average computer skills and need a simple way to write updates, but a wrong score or scorer on a public team site is worse than no site at all. The program needs a small CMS where several students can prepare content, one trusted person decides what goes public, and fans see a fast, readable, purple and white site that says when it was last updated.\n\n## Solution\n\nA local admin console (FastAPI, Jinja, SQLite) where one admin and a group of student editors log in, write updates and pages, and manage users, plus a `cms publish` step that exports only published content as static HTML for GitHub Pages. Editors can only produce drafts; the single admin reviews and publishes. The public site shows the newest updates on the home page, a navigation built from published pages (Schedule, Roster, Results/Record, History, About/Contact), and a last-updated date on everything. The admin console never goes on the internet.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As an editor, I want to log in with my own email and password, so that my work is attributed to me.\n2. As an editor, I want a clear message when my password is wrong, so that I know to retry rather than think the site is broken.\n3. As an admin, I want to log out, so that nobody else can use the shared machine under my name.\n4. As an editor, I want to log out, so that the next editor at the shared machine signs in as themselves.\n5. As an admin, I want every password stored only as a hash, so that a stolen database never reveals passwords.\n6. As an editor, I want to create an update with a title and a Markdown body, so that I can write up a game quickly.\n7. As an editor, I want the slug generated from the title automatically, so that I never have to think about URLs.\n8. As an editor, I want a duplicate slug to be resolved automatically, so that two updates with the same title do not collide.\n9. As an editor, I want a Markdown preview in the editor, so that I can check formatting before I save.\n10. As an editor, I want my new content saved as a draft, so that nothing reaches fans before the admin approves it.\n11. As an editor, I want to edit any draft, so that a teammate can fix a mistake on game night.\n12. As an editor, I want to delete my own drafts, so that abandoned drafts do not clutter the list.\n13. As an editor, I want to be blocked from deleting someone else's draft, so that nobody loses work by accident.\n14. As an editor, I want to be blocked from publishing, unpublishing, or editing published content, so that live content only changes with the admin's approval.\n15. As an editor, I want a clear \"not allowed\" screen when I try an admin-only action, so that I understand why it did not work.\n16. As an editor, I want to create and edit page drafts such as Schedule, Roster, or History, so that I can prepare content for the admin.\n17. As an editor, I want to filter the content list by status and by type, so that I can find drafts that need work.\n18. As an editor, I want a success or error message after every save, so that I know whether my change landed.\n19. As an editor, I want the admin navigation visible on every screen, so that I never get lost.\n20. As an admin, I want a dashboard showing counts of drafts, published updates, and pages, so that I see what needs review at a glance.\n21. As an admin, I want to filter the content list to drafts, so that I can review what editors wrote.\n22. As an admin, I want to publish a draft, so that it becomes eligible for the public site.\n23. As an admin, I want to unpublish published content, so that a wrong score can be pulled quickly.\n24. As an admin, I want to edit published content, so that I can correct a mistake.\n25. As an admin, I want to delete published content or pages, with a confirm step, so that I do not remove something live by accident.\n26. As an admin, I want to set each page's nav order, so that Schedule and Results appear before History and About.\n27. As an admin, I want to create a user with an email, a name, a role, and a starting password, so that a new media member can join.\n28. As an admin, I want to change a user's role, so that responsibilities can change.\n29. As an admin, I want to deactivate a user, so that a graduating media member can no longer log in.\n30. As a deactivated user, I want my past drafts and attribution kept, so that history is not rewritten.\n31. As an admin, I want the system to enforce exactly one admin, so that the club's single-admin rule is true in code.\n32. As an admin, I want a hand-over action that promotes another user and demotes me in one step, so that the role can pass on when I graduate.\n33. As an admin, I want to be prevented from deactivating or demoting myself outside of hand-over, so that the site is never left without an admin.\n34. As an admin, I want `cms publish` to render only published updates and pages, so that drafts never leave the database.\n35. As an admin, I want `cms publish` to remove content I unpublished or deleted from the exported site, so that stale content does not stay live.\n36. As an admin, I want `cms deploy` to push the export to the gh-pages branch, so that fans see the new content.\n37. As an admin, I want a short written runbook for publish and deploy, so that whoever inherits the role can do it.\n38. As a fan, I want the home page to list the newest published updates first with their dates, so that I see the latest news.\n39. As a fan, I want a navigation menu built from published pages, so that I can reach Schedule, Roster, Results, History, and About.\n40. As a fan, I want each update and page to show when it was last updated, so that I can judge whether it is current.\n41. As a fan, I want to read a match report with the verified score and scorers, so that I trust the numbers.\n42. As an alumnus, I want a History page about past titles and accomplishments, so that I can find the program's record.\n43. As a player's relative, I want a Roster page, so that I can find the player.\n44. As a fan on a phone, I want the public site and admin screens to fit without sideways scrolling, so that I can read them anywhere.\n45. As a fan, I want the site to look purple and white with a clear header, so that it feels like Kenyon.\n46. As any visitor, I want all links to work on the hosted site, so that I never hit a broken page.\n47. As any visitor, I want no script from a user's Markdown to run, so that the site is safe to open.\n48. As the admin, I want every state-changing form to carry a CSRF token, so that another website cannot act on my behalf.\n49. As a maintainer, I want sample content clearly marked as sample, so that no invented score ever looks real.\n50. As an anonymous visitor to the admin console, I want to be sent to the login page, so that nothing is exposed.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Architecture.** Follow ADR-001 and ADR-002: a local FastAPI app with server-rendered Jinja templates and SQLite, and a publish step that writes static HTML. No frontend framework and no build step.\n- **Vocabulary.** All code, templates, and tickets use the terms in `CONTEXT.md`: Update (stored as a post), Fixture, Match report, Page, Nav order, Draft, Published, Slug, Admin, Editor, Hand-over, Last updated.\n- **Users.** A user has an email, a display name, a password hash (argon2), a role (admin or editor), and an active flag. Deactivation sets the flag and never deletes the user, so authorship survives.\n- **Single admin.** Exactly one active admin exists at all times. Role changes cannot create a second admin, and the admin cannot demote or deactivate themselves. The only path is a hand-over action, which promotes the target and demotes the current admin atomically.\n- **Content.** Updates and Pages share the same core fields: title, slug, Markdown body, status (draft or published), author, created and updated timestamps. Pages add a nav order. Only two statuses exist.\n- **Slugs.** Generated from the title on first save, made unique automatically, and not editable by editors. Only the admin may change a slug.\n- **Permissions.** Editor: create content as drafts, edit any draft, delete own drafts, view the content list and dashboard. Editor may not publish, unpublish, edit or delete published content, delete another editor's draft, or reach user management. Admin: everything, including publish, unpublish, edit and delete published content, and user management. Admin-only routes return 403 for editors and redirect anonymous visitors to login.\n- **Session and login.** Cookie-based sessions. Login failures show one generic message. Deactivated users cannot log in.\n- **CSRF.** Every state-changing form carries a token that the server verifies, and a POST without a valid token is rejected.\n- **Markdown safety.** User Markdown is rendered and then sanitized with an allow-list, both in the admin preview and in the export, so script tags and event-handler attributes never execute.\n- **Admin console.** A dashboard with counts, a filterable content list (by status and by type), an editor with a Markdown preview, a user list, and persistent navigation. Every save shows a success or error message. The console is not themed beyond clear, plain styling.\n- **Publish.** `cms publish` reads only published rows and regenerates the export folder from scratch, so unpublished or deleted content disappears. Output uses relative paths only. The home page lists published updates newest first, the navigation is built from published pages by nav order, and each item shows its last-updated date. `cms deploy` pushes the export to the gh-pages branch. Both commands run from the terminal, and a short runbook is part of the documentation.\n- **Public look.** Purple and white, with a CSS-only banner header, readable at 390 px. No image files are required.\n- **Seed data.** The demo seed creates one admin, one editor, a few drafts, and a few published items. All content is clearly marked as sample, never realistic scores or stats. Credentials come from the environment.\n- **Assumptions.** A deactivated user keeps authorship and content. Updates are expected about an hour after a game. Editors use one shared machine for now.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- **What a good test is.** It asserts external behavior only: a status code, a redirect, a page's visible text, a file in the export. It never asserts on internal functions, table layouts, or template structure.\n- **Seam 1: the HTTP app.** Every capability is tested through the FastAPI test client, using the existing `client` and `client_as(role)` helpers. This covers login and logout, roles and the editor 403 and anonymous redirect on every admin-only route, content CRUD and status changes, the dashboard and filters, preview, user management, hand-over, CSRF rejection, and sanitized preview output.\n- **Seam 2: the publish export.** Run the exporter into a temporary folder and assert on the generated files: only published content is present, drafts are absent, unpublished content disappears on re-export, no root-absolute paths, navigation order matches nav order, sanitized bodies, and a last-updated date on each item.\n- **Acceptance criteria.** Each ticket's acceptance criteria map to at least one named test so the review and grading can trace them.\n- **Prior art.** The template's existing T00 test and the `client_as` fixture and its docstring examples for access-control tests.\n- **Not tested.** Visual styling and the GitHub deploy itself are checked by hand and with screenshots at 1280 px and 390 px.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Comments and moderation.\n- Live in-game scores or any server-side feature on the public site.\n- WYSIWYG editors, drag-and-drop page builders, and multi-site.\n- Remote access for editors; for now the console runs on one machine (a later change, possibly the live admin deploy stretch).\n- A \"verified result\" workflow or required source field for scores.\n- Theming the admin console.\n- Photo uploads and categories/tags are wanted but not in the core build; see Further Notes.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- **Stretch goals, after the 7 core capabilities are green and reviewed:** photo uploads with alt text, and categories and tags (for example by season or opponent). Each gets its own `stretch` issue. Each is worth 1 extra-credit point and only counts if the base score is 70 or higher.\n- **Core ticket plan.** The 7 required capabilities should split into 7 to 9 vertical tickets, each demoable alone and touching data, route, template, and test.\n- **Accuracy rule.** The client's hard rule is that the site must never show false information. That is the reason for draft-only editors, a last-updated date, clearly marked sample content, and unpublish being fast for the admin.\n- **ADR candidate.** Enforcing exactly one admin may be recorded as an ADR; this is pending the author's decision.\n- **Open item outside this spec.** `notes/cms-field-notes.md` needs at least 5 observations from WordPress Playground (S1.1) before Stage 1.\n\ntemplates/base.html\napp/auth.py\napp/db.py\napp/templating.py\napp/users.py\napp/__init__.py\napp/content.py\napp/cli.py\napp/markdown.py\napp/settings.py\napp/permissions.py\napp/main.py\napp/publish.py\ntests/test_t01_login.py\ntests/test_t04_editors.py\ntests/conftest.py\ntests/test_usage_report.py\ntests/test_ctx_guard.py\ntests/test_t05_pages.py\ntests/test_t00.py\ntests/test_t02_updates.py\ntests/test_t03_publish.py\ntemplates/admin/content_delete.html\ntemplates/admin/base.html\ntemplates/admin/refused.html\ntemplates/admin/content_list.html\ntemplates/admin/login.html\ntemplates/admin/hello.html\ntemplates/admin/content_edit.html\ntemplates/public/page.html\ntemplates/public/update.html\ntemplates/public/home.html\napp/routes/__init__.py\napp/routes/content.py\napp/routes/admin.py\napp/routes/login.py\n[project]\nname = \"iphs400-mp2-cms\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\ndescription = \"IPHS 400 MP2 — a small web CMS with a local admin console and a static public site\"\nrequires-python = \">=3.12\"\ndependencies = [\n    \"fastapi>=0.115\",\n    \"uvicorn[standard]>=0.32\",\n    \"jinja2>=3.1\",\n    \"python-multipart>=0.0.12\",   #
